name: addon-reviewer: make the publication backfill's one-time derivation crash-safe, and runnable without a full deploy
description:
Follow-up to PR 71 (`shoptet/aidev-apps`), which made the publication backfill a step of the deploy (`Backfill publication` in the `addon-reviewer` workflow, after `Verify`). Four things came out of that review and deliberately did not go into the PR: the brief ruled the backfill script's own logic out of scope, and the rest are convenience or cosmetics rather than correctness.

## 1. The one-time derivation is not transactional

`backfillPublished` (`packages/db/src/backfill-published.ts`) holds both the loop over releases and the closing `markCarriedOverBackfilled` outside a transaction — the `carried_over_backfilled_at` stamp is written at line 269, after the loop.

A run that dies mid-derivation therefore leaves some heads stamped and the stamp unset. The next run re-derives the heads it already processed, and a finding inserted on one of them in the meantime gets stamped with a release that never carried it. Nothing cleans those up — no production code ever clears `published_at` — and the symptom is that the finding gets no inline thread at its next release, because `composeReleaseReview` builds its "already published" set straight from `published_at`, independent of the carried-over switch. An inline finding has no second surface in the letter carrying its full text, so the partner effectively never sees it.

While a human ran the backfill by hand they stood over it and saw a crash immediately. Since PR 71 it runs from CI at a moment nobody picks, so the exposure is higher — which is why this is worth doing now. PR 71 answered it with documentation only (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`, the "Krok `Backfill publication` v deployi skončil červeně" entry) and the step comment.

### Watch the lock collision — this is the crux

The naive fix ("wrap the whole loop in one transaction") is worse than the problem. The backfill `UPDATE`s `review_comments`, and the live worker writes to that same table: the step runs after `Verify`, so it starts a few tens of seconds after `docker compose up -d` brought the worker up and it began taking jobs. A long transaction over that table holds locks against live traffic.

This is not theoretical — it is exactly why PR 71 gave the step `timeout-minutes: 10`. Stuck on a lock, it would otherwise sit for the job's six-hour default and hold the `addon-reviewer-deploy` concurrency group shut against every later deploy.

So the fix has to balance both. Directions worth weighing:

- a transaction around the **approximate** branch and the stamp only — the exact branch is already guarded by `isNull(publishedAt)`, so partial execution there is harmless;
- or a transaction per release rather than over the whole loop;
- or write the stamp **before** the loop and solve resumability another way.

`db.transaction` is an established pattern here (`packages/db/src/transition.ts:20`, `packages/db/src/engine-logins.ts:154`).

Note what this does **not** cover: even a successful derivation reads today's statuses, so a finding inserted on a head at any point after its send gets stamped too. That is knowingly accepted (see the file header, "Over-reporting is the direction this errs in") and this ticket does not change it. The transaction addresses the interrupted run, not the accuracy of the derivation itself.

## 2. The backfill cannot be run without a full deploy

The `addon-reviewer` workflow has a single trigger: push to master. When `Backfill publication` goes red, two paths remain:

- re-run the whole job from Actions. This also runs `Build images` and `docker compose up -d`, but it is cheap in practice — the build is cached and `up -d` does not restart containers when nothing changed. This is the currently recommended path, and PR 71 pointed the operator-facing error messages at it;
- or `qm guest exec 104 …` from erebor. `make server-backfill-published` exists but the tailnet ACL denies SSH to that VM, so the target itself does not run; the command inside it has to be copied out by hand.

`workflow_dispatch` would turn this into a button. Note that on this workflow it would by itself trigger the whole job, not just the backfill — it needs either an input plus step conditions, or a separate workflow. The `workflow_dispatch` pattern exists in the repo (`.github/workflows/error-monitoring-tool.yml`).

Lower priority than item 1: this is convenience, not correctness.

## 3. "LEFT UNTOUCHED" becomes a permanent fixture of every deploy log

**Check the premise before doing anything here** — see the note at the end.

A release sent before migration 0025 has `published_comment_ids = NULL` and always will: `setPublishedCommentIds` has a single call site (`apps/worker/src/jobs/outbound-send.ts:484`), on the path where the composer actually selected a set, and nothing backfills the column. So once the one-time derivation has run, every such release falls into `skipped++`, and the summary line ends with this on every deploy, forever:

> `; N legacy release(s) LEFT UNTOUCHED — the one-time derivation had already run, so nothing here can recover them`

That clause exists to answer one question at one moment — an operator diagnosing an adopted release wants to know whether the derivation can still recover it (see the `skipped` docblock, `backfill-published.ts:63-73`). Written for a hand-run command it is a signal; as a permanent inventory on every deploy it becomes noise, and it goes unread exactly where its author wanted it read.

**Do not "suppress the clause when nothing was derived".** `skipped` was split out of `releases - exact` precisely so that a run which derived nothing is not described as one that did; suppressing it puts half that problem back. Reword it neutrally instead.

## 4. `carried_over_backfilled_at` no longer says when the derivation ran

`markCarriedOverBackfilled` is called at the end of every run (fixed by the test "records that it ran, even with nothing to stamp"), so the value is now the last successful backfill — which, since PR 71, is usually just the last deploy. Every reader treats it as a boolean except one: `outbound-send.ts` logs it as `backfilledAt` in the adopted-release diagnosis, which is exactly where an operator wants to know when the one-time derivation ran, and the field name reads as if it answered that.

PR 71 documented the trap (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`) rather than fixing it. The fix is either to drop the field from that log line or to keep a second key holding the derivation's own timestamp.

## Check the premise first

Items 1 and 3 both depend on what production actually holds, which cannot be seen from the repo — the tailnet ACL denies SSH to the VM and postgres binds to loopback. From erebor:

```
qm guest exec 104 --timeout 60 -- /bin/sh -c 'cd /opt/addon-reviewer && docker compose exec -T postgres sh -c "psql -U \$POSTGRES_USER -d \$POSTGRES_DB -c \"select count(*) filter (where published_comment_ids is null) as legacy, count(*) as sent_total from outbound_messages where event = \$\$findings_release\$\$ and status = \$\$sent\$\$\""'
```

`legacy = 0` means item 3 can never fire and should be dropped. `legacy > 0` means it holds as written.

**Done when:** an interrupted one-time derivation cannot leave a state in which a later run stamps findings with a release that never carried them; the fix does not hold long locks on `review_comments` against the live worker, and what bounds it is stated; there is a test covering the interrupted run (`packages/db/src/backfill-published.test.ts`); the backfill can be run without a rebuild and redeploy, or the decision not to is written down; and the deploy log's steady-state output does not carry a clause that only makes sense during diagnosis.
